look_here_first: Start with one mature intact spikelet: LOWER and UPPER glumes are normally similar in length (about 18–25 mm without their terminal awns); the lower glume often shows THREE TO SEVEN veins when backlit. Then check that the plant is a wiry, freely branched ANNUAL without a persistent perennial basal crown. The open panicle and long spreading awns help, but aren't proof on their own.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays and Comal — vouchered in the Texas Hill Country grass flora; Travis — USDA/Rootfast county distribution layer records the species in Travis County.

best_field_traits: On intact mature spikelets: lower and upper glumes roughly 18–25 mm, more nearly equal in length; lower glume usually 3–7-veined (Kew GrassBase).
Annual with frequently branched wiry culms, relatively sparse widely spaced spikelets.
More cauline foliage/less persistent basal crown than A. purpurea; panicle openness overlaps.
A. purpurea: perennial persistent tuft, lower glume ~half upper glume and typically 1-veined.
wiry culms, often branched above base
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use glume relative length and LOWER glume vein count on a mature intact spikelet: A. purpurea has ~6–8 mm lower and ~11–15 mm upper (1-veined lower), while A. oligantha has ~18–25 mm subequal glumes (3–7-veined lower). Confirm a perennial vs annual basal crown; panicle shape and awn color are supporting only.
